newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets natgas transport privatization plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets natgas transport privatization plan.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) outlined on Wednesday the private natural gas distribution plan for the Mexico City federal district region and a separate zone in the surrounding suburbs.

The mammoth population and industrial center has been considered the crown jewel of the government privatization. CRE President Hector Olea estimated investment in the area would be between $900 million to $1 billion.
Mexico's oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), which formerly dominated transport, will retain exclusive control over exploration and production.

The CRE set up the two regions, according to the Official Gazette. One lies within the physical boundaries of Mexico's capital, with the second located in the sprawling Valley of Cuautitlan-Texcoco to the north and east of the city.
Mexico is privatizing natural gas transport in a move to boost use of the fuel and replace use of more polluting liquidified petroleum gas (LPG) and fuel oil.

Daily natural gas consumption in Mexico City is about 1.1 million cubic meters, or 38.5 million cubic feet. Pemex said the fuel's use in the valley region is about 2 million cubic meters, or 71.1 million cubic feet.

"Natural gas demand potential...in Mexico City is estimated at approximately 12.4 million cubic meters (439 million cubic feet) per day and in the valley of Cuautitlan-Texcoco in Mexico state more than eight million cubic meters (282 million cubic feet per day," the CRE said, citing its studies.
Olea has said that the new private transport concessionaires will need to construct new pipelines to provide natural gas to Mexico City and the outlying regions.

Currently Pemex distributes gas through three ducts of between 18 and 30 inches (45.72 to 91.44 cms) in diameter, with a total capacity of 5.4 million cubic meters (190 million cubic feet) per day. Natural gas is transported from production sites in the southeast of the country.
As of 1994, Mexico City accounted for 14.3 percent and the defined valley region was 12.5 percent of national manufacturing activity, according to National Statistics Institute (INEGI) data.

The Mexico City region covers 148,331 hectares (about 366,377 acres) and had a population of almost 8.5 million in 1995, it said. The surrounding valley zone encompasses 323,052 hectares (almost 800,000 acres) with about 8.2 million residents in 1995, it said.
Among the companies that have announced plans to submit a regional bid are Enova Corp, Pacific Enterprises, NorAm Energy Corp, France's Gaz de France Intl and Spain's Repsol SA.
